messages.subject: plotting 3D images
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I recently noticed you added support for importing 3D datasets using some of the benchmark datasets released in GigaScience. Could you tell me the function to generate 3d images, below is the code I have tried using a benchmark dataset:

require(devtools)

dev_mode(on=T)

install_github("kbemis/Cardinal")

require(Cardinal)

setwd(".../3d_benchmark")
microbe_3d<-readImzML("Microbe_Interaction_3D_Timecourse_LP")

image(microbe_3d,feature=2000,strip=FALSE,key=FALSE,colorkey=FALSE)

Which produces a series of plots for each slice of the 3D image..I also noticed the benchmark datasets include a new coordinate space for 3D imaging:

<userParam name="3DPositionX" value="5601.64"/>
<userParam name="3DPositionY" value="-11512.5"/>
<userParam name="3DPositionZ" value="0"/>

Is this coordinate space loaded into the ImageSet and used for 3D plotting? If so, how could I assign them in the msset? (I have my transformations parsed into R)

I have used the affine function for transforming my coordinates but often end up with many blank pixels from rotation.

Sorry for the ton of questions..I'm very interested to do a 3D analysis in Cardinal, especially if I can use transformations I have developed elsewhere.

Heath
